plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and align with conservative limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Exit high-beta, below-stop names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, leading to lower expected drawdowns. However, it also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to small positions.
This reduces overall risk while maintaining some growth potential.
Initiate a new position in ERY, a strong scanner long setup, for balanced growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5%/month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new, high-quality long setup. Expect moderate drawdowns with reasonable upside.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with concentration limits.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to press growth.
Initiate a new position in ERY, a strong scanner long setup, for aggressive growth.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher potential returns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, which amplifies both upside and potential drawdowns. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to boost income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for stability.
Exit all high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to reduce volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1%/month, focusing on yield and capital preservation. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, aiming for stable monthly distributions. While prioritizing income, NAV can still fall in market downturns, and distributions are variable.
